title: Investigating Cultural Alignment of Large Language Models

bias_targets.methodology: Simulating the World Values Survey by prompting models with demographic personas from the United States and Egypt, and measuring the similarity (using Soft and Hard metrics) between the models' answers and actual human ground-truth responses to identify Anglocentric representation.

Evaluating the difference in cultural alignment scores when models are prompted in the native language of a specific culture (Arabic) versus a foreign language (English), as well as analyzing the impact of pretraining data language composition.

Comparing the models' cultural alignment scores across different social classes (e.g., lower vs. upper-middle class) and education levels to measure alignment disparities for digitally underrepresented populations.
Comparing the alignment of model responses with actual survey data when the model is prompted using male versus female personas.
Measuring the differences in cultural alignment scores when the model is prompted to adopt the personas of different age groups.
